The current DDIA package has a concise general skill and source retrieval, with chapter notes outside the repository. Make its engineering capabilities portable, explicit across all 14 chapters of DDIA Second Edition, and behaviorally evaluable.

Acceptance criteria:
- Preserve ddia-skill and ddia_agent compatibility; use repository naming conventions for seven callable skills: assess, design, review, validate, migrate, operate, explain.
- Ship original concept-level references spanning all 14 chapters, with applicability, procedures, assumptions, correct/incorrect examples, falsification checks, and exact source locators. Keep progressive loading.
- Add a machine-readable concept coverage ledger linking references, workflows, examples and evaluation cases; distinguish authored guidance, tested mechanics and measured agent behavior.
- Add architecture/project handoff templates and scoped routing into project creation and consequential changes without imposing global gates.
- Improve ranked local retrieval, aliases and qualification discovery while preserving source integrity and exact citations.
- Add broad, reproducible evaluation cases, correct controls, anti-overengineering checks, controlled baseline/current/redesigned comparisons and honest limitations.
- Validate fresh installation, names, references, executable helpers and existing repository behavior; independently review and verify the completed diff.

Non-goals: unrelated PRs, global user configuration changes, claiming production correctness or benchmark superiority without measured evidence, introducing external infrastructure.

Deliver through an independently reviewed PR and merge after required checks pass.
